summary: Hart Island light in Canso Harbour, first exhibited 1872 and rebuilt 1928; its present range lights guide ships in. The boat-only flag is unverified.

light.characteristic: F R (Hart Island front range, current)

structures.status: inactive since the 1960s; lantern room removed
structures.note: Replaced the original 1872 lighthouse on Hart Island (Lighthouse Friends). No light on it in the current Coast Guard list.
Hart Island front range light (Coast Guard list).
Hart Island rear range light (Coast Guard list).

structures.name: Starling Rock
structures.note: Separate light in the harbour (Coast Guard list).

access.note: Lighthouse Friends: grounds open, tower closed; viewable from the Canso waterfront. The record's boat-only flag is not supported by a source in the file.

events.note: Catoptric fixed red light on Cutler's or Hart's Island, first exhibited 10 July 1872; keeper John Langley at $200 a year (quoted by Lighthouse Friends from the 1872 Department report).
Hydrographic survey notes say arrangements were being made for range lights to guide into the south entrance.
False Passage fixed green light on a rock at the north entrance to Canso harbour, in operation 30 December 1902.
Range light buildings erected on the south side of Canso harbour, front tower 9.8 m, back tower 13.4 m, 383 m apart.
5th-order 360-degree dioptric apparatus substituted for the catoptric apparatus at Canso Harbour (year ended 31 March 1910). Lighthouse Friends gives 1909.
Original lighthouse on Hart Island removed; combined dwelling and light built (Lighthouse Friends).
Enclosed 1928 building inactive since the 1960s (Lighthouse Friends gives no exact year; 1960 is an approximation).
Report says a storm carried the False Passage light's pole away 'last winter' (report written late 1903).
False Passage light re-established on a pole rising from a concrete pier; the light first lit 10 November 1903, 25 ft above high water.

corrections.why: The record's light values are those of Starling Rock, a separate light on a crib in the harbour. The Hart Island range shown on the Coast Guard list is F R with a 17 nm nominal range. Starling Rock values can stay as a separate entry.

corrections.current: Structures list the 1872 lighthouse as the current tower
corrections.proposed: Lighthouse of 1872 replaced by a combined dwelling and light in 1928; that building is inactive since the 1960s
corrections.why: Lighthouse Friends says the original Hart Island lighthouse was removed in 1928 and that its successor has been inactive since the 1960s. The current active lights are the Hart Island range.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Sources differ on whether the light is still lit. The 1872 building is inactive (Lighthouse Friends) while the Hart Island range and Starling Rock are active (Coast Guard list). The record's 'active' applies to the range, not the old lighthouse.

notes_for_editor: Checked 2026-10-28 against the page images. The 1909 keepers' table (scan p. 166, printed p. 159) gives 'Canso Harbour and False Passage: Joseph Long, Dec. 31, 1896' and 'Canso Harbour Range: Wm. J. Mathews, Dec. 17, 1904'. The 1911 table (scan p. 242, printed p. 235) gives the same two stations for Long and Mathews. The 1905 table (scan p. 344, printed p. 263) lists Long at Canso Harbour (31 Dec 1896) and at False Passage Ledge, and Mathews at Canso Range (17 Dec 1904). All of these were matched by line or column adjacency and confirmed on the image. The 1872 light is known only through Lighthouse Friends quoting the Department's 1872 report; that report is not in the corpus (marine_ca starts 1900). Lens date: Lighthouse Friends says 1909; the Department report for the year ended 31 March 1910 is the earliest source found for the 5th-order dioptric change; not resolved. The 1905 range towers' link to the present Hart Island and Canso Harbour range pairs is not documented, and the story says so. The False Passage light's storm and 1903 relight come from the 1903 report (scan p. 73). The 1905 report is for the fiscal year ended 30 June 1905, submitted March 1906; the story says so. The 1901 hydrographic note is the Department's surveyor's own report on the harbour survey. Dropped from the story: the schooner Clara's wreck at the harbour entrance on 20 October 1912 (Department report for the year ended 31 March 1913, scan p. 229); the life-saving crew's rescue is not tied to the light, so the story omits it and the editor may restore it as harbour context. The record's boat-only flag is not supported by any source read; the Lighthouse Friends directions go to a waterfront viewpoint in Canso, and the story says so and does not repeat the 'some listings' claim. The disputed structure positions (a 593 m disagreement between sources) were not resolved. The 1928 building is from Lighthouse Friends only. Chronicling America was not searched for this station. Lighthouse Friends gives no exact year for the lantern removal; the 1960 deactivation event is an approximation.
